newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - July 18.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Friday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Lucent Technologies Agreed to pay $1.8 billion to buy voice mail systems maker Octel Communications.
* Burlington Resources agreed to buy Louisianna Land & Exploration for about $2.44 billion.
* Hilton Hotels CEO Stephen Bollenbach may be facing his first big defeat in his pursuit of ITT, which he concedes appears to have outmaneuvered his $6.5 billion hostile bid.
* Tobacco industry delegates said they might consider changes to parts of their proposed settlement.
* The battle over Boeing 's planned merger with McDonnell was joined by President Clinton, who hinted that Washington would consider retaliation if the EU tries to block the deal.
* Barclays Bank's U.S. securities unit is the focus of a federal probe, looking at allegations that the unit improperly absorbed trading losses caused by client errors.
* Microsoft 's profit growth slowed in the fiscal fourth quarter.
* The Columbia/HCA inquiry was extended to Georgia, and doctors and consultants are being questioned about the firm's billing practices.
* Merck posted solidly higher second quarter earnings.
* Stock prices slipped as investors took a breather from their buying spree.
* McDonald's reported a four percent increase in second quarter profit.
* Network Solutions committed an error that led to one of the worst outages on the global computer network in years.
* Coca-Cola posted a 25 percent jump in secoond quarter earnings.
* MCI Communications warning of losses puts a cloud over the stock of its intended acquirer, British Telecommunications.
